title: Finite-sample near-equivalence for correlated OU sensor-response observations

model.numerical_scope: All covariance matrices in the frozen near-swap experiment are positive definite because the declared readout-noise variance is strictly positive. No jitter or covariance repair is used.

worlds.relation_to_source_world: perturb the physical decay rate of exact pole-swap World B from 4.0 to 4.04 while preserving q

sampling_design.readout_noise: independent Gaussian readout noise added to each sample
sampling_design.cost_model: one unit per acquired time sample; synthetic benchmark units only

structural_vs_practical.interpretation: The full covariance kernels differ, so the worlds are structurally distinguishable under ideal observation of the complete passive law. They remain practically near-indistinguishable under the frozen finite noisy sampling designs.

disambiguating_probe.interpretation: Under the declared two-pole model, a known step applied at the sensor inlet directly exposes the instrument response rate and strongly separates the sensor poles. This is a synthetic noiseless reference; a physical implementation must declare stimulus uncertainty and readout noise.

numerical_method.implementation_recommendation: Cholesky factorizations, triangular solves and log determinants; do not form an explicit matrix inverse
numerical_method.pinsker: TV(P_A,P_B) <= sqrt(KL(P_A||P_B)/2); it also holds with A and B reversed, so the minimum of the two valid directional upper bounds is valid
numerical_method.bayes_accuracy: for equal priors, optimal classification accuracy=(1+TV)/2; substituting the TV upper bound yields an upper bound, not an achieved classifier score
numerical_method.high_precision_reference: mpmath 60 decimal digits in the authoring runtime; source parameters and formulas are frozen here for independent replay

claim_boundary: A synthetic finite-sample Gaussian-process identifiability reference. No physical sensor calibration, traceability, QUANT result, or SOTA performance is established.

fixed_sample_count_interval_sensitivity.purpose: Explore the joint effect of temporal spacing and observation horizon at a fixed 32-sample cost. This is a finite candidate-grid comparison, not a continuous optimum.
fixed_sample_count_interval_sensitivity.interpretation: Among this declared six-point grid, sample interval 0.5 has the largest directional KL (in either direction). Very short spacing uses the same sample budget over too short a horizon; very long spacing undersamples the response dynamics. This is not a globally optimal interval and must be compared under explicit elapsed-time and acquisition-cost budgets.
